assets.defect_engineered: the bureau's flat press badge: name+organisation+track set as ONE continuous tab-delimited text story in ONE fixed-measure frame that DOES NOT SPILL (over-long strings stop rendering silently at the frame edge, page still renders); the check-in code is a DECORATIVE flat grey filled rectangle, not a picture well and not a live field; exactly two placed image graphics (portrait, mark) differentiated only by bounds+link; NO bleed box (media box = trim)
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the venue print bureau's existing flat delegate-badge press PDF (single record, flat, to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: single badge, 4 in x 3 in (101.6 x 76.2 mm) LANDSCAPE, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed on all edges), fonts fully embedded, produced through a full print engine so it converts cleanly to a native document.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (appears to be several tidy fields):
- Left column (~40% width): a PORTRAIT of the delegate, a vertical near-square photograph filling the left panel to the trim edge.
- Upper right: the DELEGATE NAME in a quiet high-contrast serif, large and calm (Paper Off White #F5F2EC text on the Deep Ink Navy #1B2733 ground on this side).
- Under the name: the ORGANISATION in a restrained sans small-caps, smaller, Warm Stone #DED6C7.
- Under the organisation: a single TRACK WORD (Operators / Capital / Policy) as a small typographic distinction in Engraved Brass #A98544 small-caps, no colour block.
- Top-right corner: the SUMMIT MARK, small, engraved-brass-coloured, sitting above the name.
- Lower right: a CHECK-IN CODE PANEL, a small square that reads like a scannable code.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The NAME line, the ORGANISATION line and the TRACK word are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame, separated by TAB characters (name \t organisation \t track), NOT three addressable frames. There is nothing to map field-by-field; the mapping must be reconstructed from the concatenated content runs and split on the tabs by computed offset.
- That single text frame is a FIXED-MEASURE frame that DOES NOT SPILL: a string longer than the measure simply stops rendering at the frame's right edge. The page still renders, the page count is still right, and nothing anywhere reports the loss. A long organisation therefore reads as a plausible shorter name with no indication anything was cut.
- There are EXACTLY TWO placed image graphics: the left PORTRAIT frame and the top-right MARK frame. In the converted document they are distinguishable ONLY by their bounds (the portrait is the large left near-square; the mark is the small top-right box) and by their link (the mark links the recovered summit artwork; the portrait link is a static placeholder face). Deciding which graphic frame holds the delegate portrait rather than the mark is a judgement against this printed reference.
- The CHECK-IN CODE PANEL is NOT a picture well and NOT a live field: it is a flat grey (#3C4148 at ~35% tint over the ground) FILLED RECTANGLE placed as a decorative graphic. It has no image link to rebind and no text to map. A merge that documents a code field against it is accepted and normalised by the validator and prepare returns success, but nothing is created and every rendered badge keeps this same flat grey rectangle.
- NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called; useDocumentBleeds is accepted but produces none, so bleed is a disclosure item, not something recoverable.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content structure, not as visible tokens): NAME | ORGANISATION | TRACK | PORTRAIT(graphic) | MARK(graphic) | CODE(decorative, not bindable)

Colours: Deep Ink Navy #1B2733 right-panel ground, Paper Off White #F5F2EC name text, Warm Stone #DED6C7 organisation, Engraved Brass #A98544 track word and mark, Graphite #3C4148 code-panel grey.
Fonts embedded: a high-contrast text serif for the name; a restrained humanist sans (small caps) for the organisation and track. These are the bureau's faces and remain the badge's typography; no font can be swapped onto this surface.

assets.prompt: Photorealistic handheld photograph, shot at a slight upward angle, of a rectangular polished BRASS lectern plate mounted on the sloped top of a dark wooden lectern in a hotel ballroom, lit by warm recessed ceiling DOWNLIGHTS so the polished brass throws bright reflections and a single BRIGHT SPECULAR HIGHLIGHT BAND lies diagonally across the plate. ENGRAVED into the brass (cut into the metal, reading as a value shift and shadow in the reflective surface rather than as printed ink, no colour contrast, only the play of light in the incised lines): a fine compound summit mark - a slim ENGRAVED CIRCLE crossed by a single vertical meridian line so the circle's interior is divided into TWO thin crescent counters, and to its right the words MERIDIAN SUMMIT in engraved small-capital letters, the word SUMMIT smaller beneath MERIDIAN, and critically the diagonal specular light band falls right across the word SUMMIT washing out part of its engraved letters. Realistic brass with fine brushed grain, faint fingerprints, warm ballroom bokeh behind, casual real-world photo, not a studio product shot.

assets.content:
MERIDIAN SUMMIT 2026 - DELEGATE TRACKS (from the producer)
Three tracks. People want to know who they are standing next to, so carry the track on the badge as a quiet typographic mark, never a colour block.
Operators - they run the network: regional transmission and grid operations.
Capital - they fund it: infrastructure funds, investors and lenders.
Policy - they regulate it: utility policy, ratepayer advocacy and commission staff.
